Transcript:
[00:00:05] Marcus Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're gonna run about 50 minutes here. quick intros?
[00:00:12] Evan Rhodes: yeah Evan, I'm CTO at GyroCloud, Marta's our cloud lead, Ravi on security and Jon is ops. thanks for setting this up.
[00:00:20] Marcus Chen: awesome. Leah, do you want to tee up the compatibility checklist?
[00:00:25] Leah Ortiz: sure, uh so we have the marketplace packaging doc — i sent a earlier draft — it's in the deck link, right now it's called "govcloud-package-v1" (link: https://redwood.ai/internal/govcloud-package-v1) um two big things up front: network egress/no public internet, and customer-managed KMS for key material. those drive a number of packaging choices.
[00:00:44] Marta Silva: when you say no public internet, does that require us to host model artifacts inside our VPC or can Redwood pull from a private S3 gateway?
[00:00:52] Leah Ortiz: good q. for GovCloud models we have two flavors: hosted artifact repo (Redwood-hosted but in gov region) or customer-hosted artifacts. in gov mode the preference is customer-hosted or a shared gov s3 we provision, because cross-regional public egress tends to be blocked.
[00:01:10] Ravi Kapoor: that aligns with our security policy — all artifacts must remain in gov region and we need customer KMS with HSM-backed keys. do you support KMS key import or external HSM?
[00:01:22] Samir Patel: briefly, yes we support both customer-managed KMS via standard KMS APIs and you can bring-your-own HSM. there's a small extra ops step for the HSM binding — we'll send the runbook. small caveat: if you choose external HSM, some of our autoscaling modes need a short-lived signing token passed to workers at boot.
[00:01:41] Jon Park: can you expand on that token flow? our policy is that no long-lived secrets are stored on host.
[00:01:46] Samir Patel: right — we exchange a short-lived cert using our control-plane handshake over a private peering channel. the handshake is initiated by a bootstrap agent that runs inside your VPC. token TTL is configurable — default 15 minutes, can be made shorter.
[00:02:01] Marcus Chen: also want to call out marketplace packaging — there are required metadata fields for GovCloud listings: compliance certs, regional endpoints, archival retention policy, and a signed SBOM for the runtime. we've got a template, i'll share.
[00:02:14] Evan Rhodes: SBOM, interesting. is that mandatory for listing?
[00:02:18] Marcus Chen: for gov listings right now yes, for review. it speeds certification.
[00:02:22] Marta Silva: what about network topologies — we run private subnets with NAT gateway disabled, only VPC endpoints. can Redwood operate with VPC endpoints only?
[00:02:31] Leah Ortiz: yes, if you provide the endpoint for S3/STS and the KMS endpoint in the gov region we can communicate over VPC peering. our control plane will be private — internally we call this Private Control Mode. small note: some telemetry is optional and can be forwarded to a collector in your VPC.
[00:02:49] Ravi Kapoor: that's important — we can't have telemetry leaving the VPC unencrypted. is there an option to route all telemetry to our Splunk instance?
[00:02:56] Alicia Park: yep we support pushing trace logs and metrics to customer endpoints via secure TLS with mutual auth. we have a simple config for Splunk HEC.
[00:03:05] [00:03:05] Marta Silva: ok thanks. next, performance — we're curious about latency and KV cache warmup with isolated subnets.
[00:03:12] Leah Ortiz: cool. so the runtime is GPU-optimized and we do KV cache sharding per instance. in private mode we keep cache-local to the worker pods — warmup depends on steady-state request patterns. for cold start you can pre-warm via a synthetic prefix workload.
[00:03:28] Evan Rhodes: pre-warm how? do you have tooling to replay a prompt set?
[00:03:33] Leah Ortiz: yes, we provide a lightweight harness (link: https://redwood.ai/tools/perf-harness) that can replay and populate KV caches across the fleet. we'll attach the instructions.
[00:03:43] Jon Park: how about batching effects? we can't have high tail-latency spikes, latency SLOs are strict.
[00:03:49] Samir Patel: we have continuous batching with latency caps — basically we will cap per-request batching windows and fall back to single-item inference if you hit SLO thresholds. you can configure the latency target per route.
[00:03:59] Marcus Chen: to be explicit — for product listings you can publish a recommended config sheet with target SLO of 100ms p99 for small prompts, but that's very workload dependent.
[00:04:10] Marta Silva: 100ms p99 across a private gov peered cluster seems optimistic unless we limit max tokens or use quantized models.
[00:04:18] Leah Ortiz: agreed — we'd recommend a quantized 4-bit or 8-bit variant for most cost-sensitive GovCloud runs. also prefix caching will help.
[00:04:26] Marcus Chen: quick interjection — are there any regulatory constraints unique to your customers we should know? (crosstalk)
[00:04:31] Ravi Kapoor: we handle regulated customers in defense and public sector, so we need FedRAMP impact levels guidance, plus strong audit logs.
[00:04:40] Alicia Park: we have a FedRAMP prep packet for customers — it outlines control mappings (NIST) and we can show audit log retention options. i'll add that to the follow-up bundle.
[00:04:49] [00:04:49] Evan Rhodes: regarding marketplace listing, what artifacts do you need from us?
[00:04:55] Marcus Chen: at minimum: product name & description, regional endpoints, SBOM, compliance badges, logo, pricing tiers, and a short deployment playbook for GovCloud. there's a specific GovCloud packaging checklist — i'll attach. (action: Marcus share)
[00:05:12] Marta Silva: about model artifacts: our legal team prefers we don't ship model files to third parties. can Redwood operate by pulling models from our internal S3 during boot?
[00:05:21] Samir Patel: yes, we support in-region pull from an S3 endpoint behind your VPC endpoint during startup; for continuous traffic we cache local copies. note: if you want zero artifact transfer, we can ship a pre-built container image to your registry with artifacts baked in, but that requires an air-gapped image transfer process.
[00:05:39] Ravi Kapoor: and the SBOM for that image? do you accept signed SBOMs from our build pipeline?
[00:05:44] Leah Ortiz: yes signed SBOMs are accepted; we prefer SPDX or CycloneDX formats.
[00:05:50] [00:05:50] Jon Park: security-wise, what's the expected network ACL configuration for the bootstrap agent? we run minimal ingress rules.
[00:05:57] Samir Patel: bootstrap requires egress to our control-plane endpoint over TLS on 443, and ephemeral ports for intra-cluster. we'll provide a minimal rule set; many customers limit to a few CIDR ranges and peering endpoints.
[00:06:11] Marcus Chen: switching gears to listing QA — there's a cert verification step we run where we stage a canary deployment in a gov test account; it's optional but recommended. does GyroCloud want us to run that?
[00:06:22] Evan Rhodes: yes, please — that'll help our compliance team validate.
[00:06:25] Marta Silva: timeline wise, if we aim for an internal pilot in June, when should we start the bench?
[00:06:31] Leah Ortiz: i would say start baseline perf this month — week of May 25 — run 3 scenarios (small prompt low tokens, medium prompt burst, and long token generation). should take 2-3 days per scenario.
[00:06:43] Marcus Chen: noted. Leah will own the harness and configs.
[00:06:47] [00:06:47] Customer: (inaudible)
[00:06:50] Marta Silva: quick question on billing and marketplace metering — will tokens be metered per-model variant or per-route?
[00:06:58] Marcus Chen: marketplace billing can be configured per-route; for dedicated/private offerings we can meter either per-token or per-session depending on contract. for GovCloud marketplace listing we typically show a tokens-per-1000 cost estimate.
[00:07:11] Ravi Kapoor: any competitors who have done GovCloud already?
[00:07:14] Marcus Chen: some vendors like CloudRunX have listings but they usually do limited features; MegaServe did a bigger integration but had issues with KMS integration. we'll go into those lessons in follow-up.
[00:07:26] [00:07:26] Samir Patel: ok dive into the perf knobs — batching, quantization, and KV cache.
[00:07:31] Leah Ortiz: first, batching: set a max latency window (ms) and a max batch size; we also allow dynamic batching by request type. second, quantization: 4-bit/8-bit tradeoffs — 4-bit offers big cost wins but some quality delta on long-form; third, KV cache: prefix caching reduces per-token compute but increases memory footprint.
[00:07:56] Marta Silva: can you give ballpark throughput numbers for c5/8 gpus in gov region?
[00:08:03] Samir Patel: in gov regions we usually map to a1-like GPU types — rough numbers: small-medium model variant ~ 100-400 reqs/sec per pod (depending on tokens and batch). we'll validate with your workload in the baseline.
[00:08:18] Jon Park: latency and cold starts remain a concern. do you support instance warm pools?
[00:08:24] Leah Ortiz: yes, warm pools — reserved instances in Dedicated/Gov mode can remain hot. for marketplace quickstarts we recommend configuring a small warm pool during peak traffic.
[00:08:34] [00:08:34] Ravi Kapoor: about audit logging — can you provide immutable logs with append-only digest? we need tamper-evident trails.
[00:08:41] Samir Patel: we support signed append-only logs that you can ship to your archival store; there's a digest verification tool. we'll include the docs.
[00:08:50] Marcus Chen: time check we're about 9 minutes in — lots of good stuff. any open blockers we should capture?
[00:08:57] Evan Rhodes: from our side: need to confirm image/artifact transfer policy with legal, and confirm HSM procurement timelines.
[00:09:05] Marta Silva: and we need the VPC peering template and port list.
[00:09:09] Marcus Chen: got it. Leah/Samir/Alicia will compile package.

[00:09:42] Marta Silva: terraform snippet — do you have a canonical example for gov peering + endpoint config?
[00:09:48] Leah Ortiz: yes, we have a repo with examples — i'll paste link in chat (https://redwood.ai/examples/gov-terraform). it's opinionated but a good starting point.
[00:09:57] Jon Park: will the example cover route tables and security group rules?
[00:10:02] Leah Ortiz: yep, it includes route tables, peering, security groups and NACL suggestions.
[00:10:07] [00:10:07] Marcus Chen: on the marketplace listing UI side, there is a vetting step where our listing team will request a short recorded demo of the deployment. we typically ask for a 5-8 minute screencast.
[00:10:18] Evan Rhodes: we can produce that.
[00:10:21] Marcus Chen: perfect. any questions on the licensing model?
[00:10:24] Marta Silva: will there be a separate enterprise contract for GovCloud or the standard marketplace T&Cs apply?
[00:10:30] Alicia Park: marketplace listings start under standard T&Cs, but enterprise customers often add an enterprise addendum. legal will walk through options.
[00:10:38] [00:10:38] (keyboard clacking)
[00:10:45] Leah Ortiz: ok moving into perf baseline plan specifics: we recommend three scenarios (as mentioned). we'll provide a small harness that can be run from within your VPC — it uses a synthetic workload and measures p50/p95/p99, token/sec, and KV cache hit rates.
[00:11:03] Marta Silva: are there any dependencies on external services for the harness? we try to keep everything internal.
[00:11:07] Leah Ortiz: none — everything runs in-VPC; the harness only needs to reach the worker endpoints and the control-plane peering for bootstrap.
[00:11:15] Ravi Kapoor: regarding monitoring, which metrics should we expose to our SREs?
[00:11:20] Samir Patel: key metrics: token throughput, avg latency, p99 latency, KV cache hit ratio, GPU utilization, and batch sizes. we can export all of these via prometheus and push to your metrics ingestor.

[00:11:39] Evan Rhodes: would you run the eval or we run it?
[00:11:42] Leah Ortiz: we can run it as part of the baseline if you give us the prompt set and expected outputs; otherwise we'll share the eval harness for you to run.
